scope: One local validation startup timeout; no production transport fix is claimed.

initial_run.test: native-h3: request FIN and automatic destruction preserve a queued 20 MiB response
initial_run.process_disposition: The owner terminated the failed test process after diagnostic capture; this run was not counted as passing.

comparison_to_hosted_source.note: Only the installed-consumer warning assertion changed; production code and the failing lifecycle/WASM tests were identical.

diagnosis.method: Read-only Node inspector state and closure scopes, socket inventory, and a short native thread sample captured before termination.
diagnosis.confirmed_phase: The fixture was awaiting connectAsync; its session binding had not initialized.
diagnosis.confirmed_no_transfer: The server handler variables raw and sending were undefined; no request stream or response pipeline had been created.
diagnosis.confirmed_cleanup_defect: The fixture registered t.after only after connectAsync returned, leaving the already-started server unowned when connection startup timed out.
diagnosis.connection_timeout_cause: Unknown. The evidence does not distinguish a DNS, handshake, socket, scheduling, or other startup cause.
diagnostic_limits: The failed client object was no longer retained when inspected; its close error was unavailable.
Native lifecycle tracing was disabled, so no per-connection history was available.
Aggregate native telemetry recorded zero driver setup failures, runtime-error exits, sink errors, and dropped events; these counters do not identify the timeout cause.

changes: Register cleanup before listen and connect awaits.
Close the server in finally even if session cleanup fails.
Pass the test abort signal into connectAsync.
cleanup_fix.regression: Cancel a pending connection during DNS resolution, require AbortError, then rebind both TCP and UDP on the released server port.

followup_validation.interpretation: Successful repeats and final suites did not reproduce the startup timeout. They verify the cleanup fix and exercised transfers; they do not establish or eliminate the original connection-startup cause.
